assets.prompt: Paint a new production background plate for a 2D fantasy RPG command chamber, opaque 1536 × 1024 landscape. Orthographic three-quarter overhead, screen-square geometry, crisp hand-painted mineral-blue slate, aged brass, tiny warm highlights. Critical level design: the upper TWO THIRDS of the entire canvas is uninterrupted, plain dark dressed stone from the extreme left edge to the extreme right edge. It is the mounting surface for a wall-to-wall bank of live displays added by the game. Absolutely no doors or side corridors in this upper region. The ONLY two tunnel entrances are down in the BOTTOM LEFT and BOTTOM RIGHT corners, entirely below y=700. Think of the bottom third as a horizontal cross-corridor. A small, substantial, stone-vaulted tunnel is cut into each short end of that lower corridor, its walkable threshold at about 90% of image height. West tunnel under an amber lantern, east tunnel with cool turquoise crystal light. Each entrance is contained in the outermost 12% of the image, with a deep readable black interior, tactile stone arch blocks and bright edging, facing inward from the left and right so a character walks LEFT or RIGHT into them from the center foreground. The two entrances must be conspicuous in the lower corners, framed inside the canvas and connected by a continuous broad band of level slate flagstones. The foreground center stays quietly detailed and open for sprites and four interactive floor controls. Very bottom center opens smoothly toward the viewer. Low, restrained copper inlays follow the paving toward each mouth. Camera composed as a real adventure-game room, glowing cave light, atmospheric but readable floor, rich material details at the two tunnel thresholds. No people, silhouettes, consoles, black screen rectangles, HUD, lettering, labels, map symbols, foreground obstructions or stairs. Full-bleed single room.
edits: Edit this game background's vertical layout. Keep the slate-and-brass art style, amber left arch and turquoise right arch. IMPORTANT: move the entire strip of architectural detail and both arched doorways much LOWER. The final 1536x1024 game composites a rectangular screen over all pixels y=77 through y=697, across the entire image width. Anything above y=700 WILL BE COVERED. Both lit arches, their lights and all the decorative stone framing must fit ENTIRELY BELOW y=704 in the finished image so both will remain visible. The top of each lantern and the highest stone at y=710. The black entrances centered at x=90 and x=1446, their thresholds at about y=935. The chambers should read as lower-left/lower-right CORNER exits across the same traversable horizontal band, use bold big dark door holes at least one small game character tall. Paint a lower/bigger block of completely plain uninterrupted dark slate wall occupying the first 70 percent, like empty dark negative space. Compress and shift the architecture down as needed to respect this position. Lower the wall/floor junction to about y=835 then bring the side tunnels forward of it, connected by softly lit stone floor across the bottom foreground. Keep the small warm brass inlay. No visual or structural elements in the upper 70% besides flat slate masonry, even along the far left or right edges. Full bleed, same crop and resolution. No painted monitors or UI, no text, no characters.

Final in-place art edit to this 1536×1024 RPG level. Preserve both small doorway arches and their lamps in exactly the same lower-corner positions and at the same sizes (thresholds around x=90 and x=1446, y=935). Preserve the plain upper wall across the image. Change the FLOOR ONLY. Right now there is only a thin strip of paving at the bottom, while the characters would need to walk on the vertical wall. Paint an extensive FLAT, broad slate flagstone floor across the bottom THIRD of the picture, with the floor beginning at y=695 (68 percent of the way down), exactly level across the middle of the canvas. The horizontal baseboard and the junction between the vertical wall and the ground in the middle must move UP from y=919 to y=695! Between the two arches the entire area from y=700 to the absolute bottom is horizontal paved ground, with dressed flagstones getting smaller toward the top for perspective, tasteful worn brass inlays, small polished spots of amber and teal light near the tunnels. Paint flanking SHORT side walls receding from each doorway on the extreme left and right, going up-screen behind the arches to the same raised floor-wall junction, so the arches are still in the bottom corners opening onto the floor. The ground begins BEHIND both entrances; they are side exits in an open courtyard. Keep the blue-slate, amber and turquoise palette, hand-painted fantasy game texture and orthographic three-quarter camera. Leave all space clear for player sprites, terminals and furniture added at runtime. No objects on floor, no people, text, screens, UI, signs or new doorways.

Edit this 1536×1024 hand-painted game background. The game designer wants BOTH lower corner tunnel exits visibly raised by a modest but unmistakable amount, about 65 game pixels. Do this by redrawing the entrances slightly farther back along the short side walls, facing slightly toward the center. The walkable mouths must open onto the higher level row of paving, about 86% down the canvas (threshold y=880–890 instead of y=955). Leave a full clear strip of uninterrupted stone pavement about 125–140 pixels tall from the portals' thresholds down to the very bottom, so a character standing in the lower right is beside and below the doorway. Put the right arch slightly further toward the right edge, with the black doorway centered around x=1460; put the left one centered symmetrically around x=76. Both silhouettes remain fully in frame. Keep the clear width and height inside each arch; solid stacked stone, a convincing deep dark interior, crisp amber lamp on the left arch and cyan lamp on the right. Rehang their lanterns on shorter side brackets at about y=725; lamps, arch crowns and ALL door details must remain below y=700 because a full-width in-game screen plugs in above that line. Instead of keeping floor-border lines in the old positions, repaint continuous stone paving where the doorways used to be, with a new bronze crescent threshold at the base of each raised opening. Keep center floor geometry and horizontal rear-wall baseline, the full-width uninterrupted dark slate wall above, and general look of the provided image. The two new entrances belong HIGHER within the lower third, not at the very bottom. Only these two doors. Entire lower 12% reads as clear floor in front of both doorways. No figures, furniture, text, monitors or interface.

Produce the final registered background for this fantasy RPG, by interpolating the two versions provided. The first reference has doors too low; the second has doors too high for the illuminated arch to remain below the runtime screen. Keep the back wall, flagstone floor and camera unchanged. Put the two complete doorway structures, including lamps and doorstep, HALFWAY between the two referenced heights. In the original reference the lantern begins at 72% of the image and the door hits the floor at 94%. In reference 2 the lantern begins at 63% and the door hits the floor at 83%. Place final lanterns at 70%, and final door thresholds at 88% of the image height, with a clear 12% of floor in front that runs from the thresholds all the way to the bottom edge. The very top of the image through 69% must have only plain slate wall, continuous across the entire width with NO lamps, stone arches or raised corners. LOWER the tops of the tall side walls in the second image, rehang the lights on the jambs beside the arches, not on top of the arches, so nothing is clipped by the display wall over the entire top 69%. Visible vault tops at 73%, thresholds 88%, outer 13% at each side, black central holes, amber lantern on left, cyan lantern on right, attached to the inner-facing side jambs. Level floor in center starts at about 72%. All parts grounded on the open floor, walk freely left and right, naturally painted bronze inlay around each mouth. No objects, characters, text or displays; those are drawn separately by the game. 1536 x 1024. Preserve the source style exactly.
